book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Men are endlessly mad with costume fitting

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final letter, so the word just before is cut short
mad suggests things thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
the word loses its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Men are going crazy at a costume fitting session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like part of 'costume fitting' at a tailor's, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Commensurate means in proportion or corresponding, so appropriate or suitable, as something fitting is.

parts.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary
E is the abbreviation for English
red is a common label for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A celebrated left-wing English figure who led a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cheered is to be greeted with shouts of approval, that is, acclaimed.

indicators.note: embracing means holding something inside one's arms, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a moue is a little pout
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A timid little person pulling a sulky face while hugging someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a figurative term for a quiet, timid, retiring person.

parts.note: surface reading: a heart fluttering or palpitating with nerves
setter's reading: the central point of an earthquake, a tremor of the ground

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a racing pulse; 'tremor' is the seismic kind, and 'heart' its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the earth's surface directly above the focus of an earthquake, so its heart.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: coated with a first layer of plaster or render, as a wall is

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests a drunk carried out of a pub; plastered is the builder's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall rendered is given a coat of plaster, and a service rendered is one performed.

clue.text: Bird chasing the man for rent

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A bird pursuing someone who owes rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chasing' puts the bird in front, with the man following behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid to support the church, a levy much like a rent.

indicators.note: something affected has been acted upon and altered, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with a pretentious way of carrying themselves dresses up for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected manner' reads as one phrase meaning pretension; split it, and 'Affected' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to decorate or embellish it, to dress it up.

clue.text: Command from top to carry explosive

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: top as an adjective, meaning best
HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: An order from headquarters to transport explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in at the King's behest.

clue.text: Rio settled with United showing wisdom

indicators.note: things that have settled have shifted into a new position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rio (Ferdinand) settling in at Manchester United shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio Ferdinand was a Manchester United footballer, which makes 'United' read as the club rather than plain letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep learning gained from study, a loose synonym of wisdom.

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the language named first is placed second, after the other piece
initially points to the opening letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the first letter
Erse is the Irish Gaelic language

explanation.surface: An Irishman says little about the Troubles, the Northern Irish conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' places the Irish language after the first letter of Troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech uses very few words, which is what terse means.

clue.text: It's used for dodgy smoking jacket!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cannabis cigarette, smoked illicitly
second meaning: a thick double-breasted jacket of the kind sailors wear

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoking jacket' reads as one garment; split it, and smoking belongs to the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a joint of marijuana and also names a short naval-style jacket.

clue.text: Philosopher takes jug of noxious liquid

indicators.note: takes means one word gets the other inside it

parts.note: a sage is a wise man or philosopher
a ewer is a large water jug

explanation.surface: A philosopher like Socrates drinks a cup of poison.
explanation.walkthrough: The jug goes inside the philosopher after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewerage is waste water carried away in drains, an unpleasant and harmful fluid.

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Someone stingy in outlook, never lavish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as stingy, which fits 'not extravagant'; it is the verb meaning to signify.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to indicate or signify it, which is what a word means.

clue.text: Marine tuna, fresh, one caught on a line

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made over in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sea fish, freshly landed, one hooked on a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to the sea and sailing, which is what marine means as an adjective.

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
blest, an old form of blessed, as in blest with talent: provided with it

explanation.surface: Asking about the smallest, meanest wage anyone could be given.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'provided' must be read as BLEST, the old spelling, rather than its usual sense of 'if'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means weak or meagre; the superlative of feeble describes the weakest, most pitiful thing.

indicators.note: containing marks the next item as held between the two words around it

parts.note: a boom is a loud blast
E is the symbol for energy
rang is the past tense of ring, to resound

explanation.surface: A bullet bounces off a wall, and the bang echoes with force.
explanation.walkthrough: Energy sits between the blast and the word for resounded.
explanation.definitionFit: To boomerang is to recoil or rebound on the originator, as a ricochet bounces back.

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about a cheap, messy jumble sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche can be a hotchpotch or medley, a mixture of pieces from different sources.

clue.text: Offended, getting stretch say, for pot

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the words and listen to how they come out

parts.note: sore means offended or aggrieved
a span is a stretch of time or distance

explanation.surface: Someone offended at being handed a prison stretch for possessing cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with no R sounded, 'sore span' is spoken almost exactly like the kitchen word. 'Pot' and 'stretch' suggest drugs and jail; pot is the cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a deep cooking pot with a long handle, used on the hob.

indicators.note: taking means receiving something inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
lee is shelter, cover from the wind

explanation.surface: A sluggish mole burrowing for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The mole looks like the burrowing animal, but it is the espionage sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy means drowsy and slow, so lethargic in manner.

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: boots are kicks, blows given with the foot
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone knocks around the curtained bays on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Hospital's letter goes inside the word for kicks, just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Booths are small enclosed compartments, such as polling or phone booths, so cubicles.

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
to range is to sort or arrange in order

explanation.surface: An oddball character spotted out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric sort' reads as a person; split it, and 'sort' is the verb. In a down clue 'seen on' puts the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange means odd or unusual, which describes eccentric behaviour.

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters alter their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A driver shifting gear decides it is time to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time to leave' reads as one phrase; 'time' is fodder and only 'to leave' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's own country to settle permanently in another.

clue.text: Suspicious case of eructation from stomach!

parts.note: rum means odd or suspicious

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A worrying belch rising from the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: Eructation is belching; only its first and last letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumen is the first stomach of a cow or other ruminant.

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so take the opening letter

parts.note: the first letter
an error is a blunder

explanation.surface: A scandal: a shocking gaffe by the head of the Conservative party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tory leader' looks like a party chief, but it only supplies the first letter, which goes in front of the blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is intense fear, the kind of shock that leaves a person frightened.

clue.text: Power of Government head in control

indicators.note: in places the selected letter inside the other word

parts.note: a rein is a means of control

indicators.note: the head is the top, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter

explanation.surface: The power of a head of government who is in control.
explanation.definitionFit: A reign is a period of sovereign rule, so the exercise of power.

indicators.note: not starting means the word begins without its opening letter

parts.note: a moral is the lesson a story teaches

explanation.surface: A pupil told not to begin the lesson until the exam is set.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, as in a language exam.

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: the palm is the inner part of the hand
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: Passing round the hymn books at the Sunday service.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm is one of the sacred songs in the Bible's Book of Psalms, sung in worship as a hymn is.

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
America is one example of a nation; 'perhaps' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: America's place after a car factory was built there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auto plant' reads as a car factory; split it, and 'plant' is the definition. 'After' puts the nation after the car.
explanation.definitionFit: The carnation is a flowering garden plant with frilled pink, red or white blooms.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: information, as in getting the dope on someone

explanation.walkthrough: Dope usually means a fool, the opposite of brains; here it is slang for inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both secret information gathered by spies and the mental ability to understand things.
